audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart disagreed across layers on every row, and the content layer's own win[] flips were one row out of step with its whys[]: win[4] (Level 6) said Cassiopeia while whys[4] said 'Level 6 flips to him', and win[5] (First item) said Zed while whys[5] said 'Your first item swings it back to you'.
audit.why: Death Mark unlocks at level 6 — that row is Zed's. Cassiopeia's Seraph's/Liandry's spike is the first-item row and takes it back. The full layer already had phases[4].side = Zed, agreeing with the whys; the win[] pair was the offset one.
audit.corrected: Chart settled at Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Zed, Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why was the generic 'Petrifying Gaze online — the all-in answer' template sitting under a Zed side.
audit.why: Level 6 is Zed's spike, not Cassiopeia's, in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Death Mark's untargetable 625 dash and its 3-second mark.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three fields claim Death Mark has 'damage reduction'. Riot's text gives it no damage reduction at all — it makes Zed untargetable during the dash and repeats a portion of the damage he dealt while the mark was up. The content layer also names Zed's W 'Shadow Rush'; it is Living Shadow.
audit.why: enemyKit R text and W text; packet.suspectNames flags 'Shadow Rush'.
audit.corrected: whys[5], spikes[2].text and late rewritten around the 3-second mark timer instead of a reduction that does not exist; Living Shadow used in late and wants.foe[2].

audit.why: It is the field that carries real numbers.
audit.corrected: Death Mark 120s with a 3s mark, Living Shadow 20s, Shadow Slash 5s at rank 1, Razor Shuriken 75 energy.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Bodies did not match their titles.
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now states the facing requirement on Petrifying Gaze — it stuns only enemies facing you and merely slows the rest, which is exactly what the title promised.

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze online — the all-in answer. Face-stun his engage or slow his retreat; either way the fangs finish it.
edits.after: Death Mark online: he goes untargetable, dashes 625, and the mark repeats his damage 3 seconds later — his best window.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Zed wins by dropping a shadow behind you, marking you with Death Mark, and repeating three seconds of damage.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Check it before every step-up. - R Petrifying Gaze is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Death Mark is 120s at rank 1 and the mark triggers 3s after it lands — survive those 3 seconds and he has nothing. - Living Shadow is 20s and the swap is his escape. - Shadow Slash is 5s at rank 1 and it is what slows you.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by surviving one window: Zhonya's plus a faced Petrifying Gaze answers Death Mark, and the fangs do the rest.

edits.before: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, zone Zed off the wave with fang threat, and call your jungler — your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, keep him under half health so no Death Mark is worth casting, and call your jungler — grounded shadows do not escape.

edits.before: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Miasma grounds: drop it where his shadow dash lands and he arrives slowed, poisoned, and without the step-in he planned.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Zed is executable.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing you — turn into the dive and he is stone; turn away and he takes a slow and kills you.

edits.before: Zed whiffs Death Mark and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Razor Shuriken costs 75 energy at rank 1 — make him spend it.

edits.before: That is Zed’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Miasma is your only answer to the dive; the wave never needed a 20-second cooldown.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: Chasing him out of your own poison hands him the shadow swap and 290-range Shadow Slash for free — stand in your zone.

edits.before: Track Zed’s Death Mark: The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Death Mark (120s at rank 1): the mark repeats his damage 3 seconds after it lands, so what you survive is the timer, not the dash.

edits.before: Your first item swings it back to you — your DoT output alone threatens to kill through his ult's damage reduction.
edits.after: Your first item swings it back — Seraph's DoT output alone threatens to kill him inside the three seconds his mark needs.

edits.before: With your first completed item your DoT damage alone can threaten to kill him through his ult's damage reduction, and Zhonya's or QSS timing becomes the deciding factor in any full trade.
edits.after: With your first completed item your DoT alone can kill him inside the 3 seconds before Death Mark triggers, and Zhonya's timing on that mark becomes the deciding factor in any full trade.

edits.before: Your first item spike lets your DoTs threaten to outright kill him even through Death Mark's damage reduction, so you keep winning skirmishes as long as you play around cooldowns. But a fed Zed becomes the bigger threat in extended games — Youmuu's active and Shadow Rush let him dodge your Petrifying Gaze cast and reset a combo onto you before your team can react, so if he's snowballed off kills elsewhere the late-game 1v1 (and pick potential) swings back to him.
edits.after: Your first item spike lets your DoTs kill him inside the three seconds before Death Mark triggers, so you keep winning skirmishes as long as you play around cooldowns. But a fed Zed becomes the bigger threat in extended games — Youmuu's active and a Living Shadow placed behind him let him leave your Petrifying Gaze cone and reset a combo onto you before your team can react, so if he's snowballed off kills elsewhere the late-game 1v1 and pick potential swing back to him.

edits.before: Roam using Shadow Rush to shadows placed pre-emptively when you're pushed in
edits.after: Roam using Living Shadow swaps off shadows placed while you're pushed in

notes: The chart needed a real decision, not a copy: the content layer's win[] flips were one row out of step with its own whys[] (win[4]=Cassiopeia under a why that says level 6 flips to Zed; win[5]=Zed under a why that says the first item swings it back). packet.levelChart just mirrors the wrong win[]. I settled it on the kit — Death Mark unlocks at 6, Seraph's lands after — and the full layer's phases[4].side already read Zed, which corroborates it. So win[4] and win[5] are swapped and the full sides moved to match; phases[4].side needed no edit (already Zed) and phases[5].side is paired with the win[5] edit in this proposal. phases[4].why was rewritten in the same proposal because it described Cassiopeia winning that row. 'Shadow Rush' is a fabricated name for Living Shadow. 'Death Mark's damage reduction' is a fabricated mechanic — Riot's text gives the ultimate untargetability on the dash and a 3-second mark that repeats damage, no reduction — and it had propagated into three content fields.
